evals.prompt: Add logging to OrderService: log Information when an order is placed (include the order ID and total amount), and log a Warning when a retry happens (include the attempt number and max retries).
evals.expected_output: Uses [LoggerMessage] source-generated partial methods with strongly-typed parameters (int orderId, decimal total, int attempt, int maxRetries), correct log levels (Information for placed, Warning for retry), no string interpolation, no ToString(), named placeholders.

evals.prompt: Add error logging in PaymentProcessor for a failed payment (include the order id, the error code, and the exception), plus a debug log inside the loop that processes each line item (include the SKU and quantity).
evals.expected_output: Uses [LoggerMessage] delegates for both the error and debug log; exception passed as a typed Exception parameter (not ex.ToString()); error code passed as its own typed parameter, not concatenated/interpolated; debug log uses Debug level for the per-item loop.

evals.prompt: Clean up the logging in ShipmentTracker.cs — it's inconsistent and I think there might be some performance issues with it.
evals.expected_output: Migrates all four log calls to [LoggerMessage] partial methods, makes the class partial, removes string interpolation and string concatenation, removes ToString() calls on the exception and CarrierResponse, converts positional placeholders {0}/{1} to named placeholders.

evals.prompt: DataImportService has three places that need a failure log (parsing, validating, applying a record) — fill in the TODOs with appropriate logging.
evals.expected_output: Uses one deliberately-scoped, reusable [LoggerMessage] delegate (parameterized by e.g. a stage/operation name and the record identifier) rather than three near-identical bespoke delegates (LogParseFailure/LogValidationFailure/LogApplyFailure); chooses Warning level consistently; not overly chatty.
